introduction:
House and Land Documents typically refer to Property Registration, which is a mandatory process governed by the Registration Act, 1908. Registering your property ensures legal ownership and protects against disputes in Delhi.

The registration process involves paying stamp duty and registration fees, and must be completed at the local Sub-Registrar's Office within 4 months of the execution of the sale deed. It serves as an undeniable record of title and rights over the property.
quickFacts:
Important to Know (2026 Updates)
  • Official Portal: ngdrs.delhi.gov.in (Note: The old DORIS portal is no longer used for booking new appointments; all Sub-Registrar offices have migrated to NGDRS).
  • Stamp Duty:
    • Male Buyer: 6% of property value (or circle rate, whichever is higher)
    • Female Buyer: 4% of property value
    • Joint (Male + Female): 5% of property value
  • Registration Fee: 1% of the total value + ₹100 pasting charge.
  • Processing Time: 15–30 days for final deed collection.
  • Mode: Online application + Mandatory physical visit.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Property Registration

Note: Carry original documents and one set of photocopies to the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO).
Property Documents
  • Original Sale Deed (Drafted & printed on e-Stamp paper).
  • Previous Chain of Title Documents (Mother Deed, Allotment Letter, etc.).
  • NOC (No Objection Certificate) if applicable (e.g., from RWA or for agricultural land).
Proof of Identity & Address

Required for Buyer, Seller & 2 Witnesses:

  • Aadhaar Card (Mandatory).
  • PAN Card (Mandatory for transactions over ₹5 Lakh).
  • Alternate ID: Voter ID, Passport, or Driving License.
Financial Proofs
  • E-Stamp Paper (Proof of stamp duty payment).
  • E-Registration Fee Receipt (Payment acknowledgment).
  • TDS Certificate (if property value > ₹50 Lakh, TDS @ 1% must be deducted).
Others
  • Two passport-sized photos for all parties (Buyer, Seller, Witnesses).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Application via NGDRS

Important: You cannot walk directly into the office. You must book a slot online via the new NGDRS portal.
Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Buy E-Stamp Paper: Visit the Stock Holding Corporation of India (SHCIL) website or an authorized bank/vendor. Pay the calculated stamp duty (e.g., 6% or 4%). You will receive a unique E-Stamp Certificate number. Keep this safe.
  2. Step 2: Register on NGDRS Portal: Go to ngdrs.delhi.gov.in. Click "Citizen Registration" to create an account. Login and select "Property Registration".
  3. Step 3: Fill Property Details:
    • General Info: Select the District and Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) location.
    • Property Valuation: Enter property details (area, floor, usage) to auto-calculate the official valuation.
    • Party Details: Enter details for the Presenter (usually buyer), Executant (seller), and Claimant.
  4. Step 4: Upload Documents: Upload PDF scans of IDs, PAN cards, and the draft Deed.
  5. Step 5: Pay Registration Fee: Pay the 1% Registration Fee + ₹100 online through the portal’s payment gateway. Save the receipt.
  6. Step 6: Book Appointment: Once payment is confirmed, the system will show available slots for your specific SRO. Select a date and time. Download/Print the "Appointment Slip" and "Summary Report" generated.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical Visit (Offline Process)

On the day of your appointment:
  1. Step 1: Arrive Early: Reach the Sub-Registrar Office at least 15 minutes before your slot.
  2. Step 2: Facilitation Counter: Present your Appointment Slip at the reception/facilitation counter to get your token number.
  3. Step 3: Verification & Biometrics: The Sub-Registrar will verify your original IDs and the E-Stamp paper. The Buyer, Seller, and Witnesses will be called to the desk for thumb impressions and webcam photos.
  4. Step 4: Signing: Sign the deed in the presence of the officer.
  5. Step 5: Receipt: You will be given a final receipt with a "Registration Number."
afterApplying:
After Applying - Next Steps & Tracking

Tracking

Use the registration number to track your application status on the NGDRS portal.

Collection

After 1–2 weeks (timeline varies by SRO), revisit the office to collect the original Registered Sale Deed.

Mutation

Once you have the registered deed, apply for Mutation (name change in municipal records) at the MCD office to become the legal owner for tax purposes.
